findings.title: Busy times are ignored on days with a date override, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override range, the function hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (line 133) before the busy-time check at the bottom of the function. This means that on any day where a fixed host has a date override, that host's existing bookings and calendar busy times are never consulted — the slot is reported as available even if the host is already booked at that exact time. Before this change, checkIfIsAvailable always evaluated `busy`, so this is a regression that can produce double bookings for fixed hosts (and for round-robin hosts via the looseHostAvailability path, which uses the same function). The new tests don't cover the combination of a date override plus an existing booking, so this passes the suite unnoticed.

findings.title: Working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
findings.body: In the new working-hours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` (lines 141-142). Because `end` equals `start`, the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never detect a slot that starts inside working hours but finishes after they end. For example, with working hours 09:00-17:00 and a 60-minute event, a slot starting at 16:30 (ending 17:30, outside availability) passes the check and the fixed host is treated as available. This undermines the very guarantee this PR is adding — that slots are only shown when fixed hosts are actually available.

findings.title: Working-hours `find` logic is wrong both ways: valid slots rejected and non-working days accepted
findings.body: The working-hours check uses `workingHours.find(...)` where the callback returns true only when a matching-day entry excludes the slot. Two failure modes follow. (1) If a host has split working hours on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00), a slot at 10:00 is not excluded by the first block but IS excluded by the second block (`start 600 < 840`), and `find` short-circuits on that second block — so a slot genuinely inside working hours is reported unavailable. The logic needs to require that the slot is within at least one block, not that no block excludes it. (2) If none of the host's working-hour entries include the slot's day at all, `find` returns undefined and the slot falls through to the busy check as available — so for a round-robin event (where aggregated working hours union all hosts' days), a fixed host who doesn't work that day at all is still considered available and the event can be booked with them, which is exactly the class of bug this PR claims to fix.

findings.title: `===` comparison of two Dayjs objects is always false (dead code for unavailable-day overrides)
findings.body: Line 114 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')`. These are two freshly created Dayjs object instances, so strict reference equality is always false and this branch never executes. The intent is clearly to detect full-day 'unavailable' date overrides (start == end, stored as 00:00-00:00). Because the branch is dead, detection relies on the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` check, which misses a slot starting exactly at the override boundary time (e.g. midnight for a blocked day): such a slot makes the find callback return falsy, sets dateOverrideExist=true, and is then returned as available with busy checks skipped. Use `.isSame()` instead of `===`.

findings.title: Slot starting exactly at a date override's end is treated as inside the override
findings.body: The boundary check uses strict `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))` (line 123). A slot that begins exactly when the override ends (e.g. override 14:00-18:00, slot 18:00-18:45) is not excluded by this condition nor by the earlier `slotEndTime.isBefore/isSame(start)` condition, so the find callback returns falsy, `dateOverrideExist` remains true, and the function returns 'available' — additionally skipping the busy check due to the early return at line 133. The condition should be `!slotStartTime.isBefore(end)` so a slot at the exact override end is excluded.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion silently breaks when `timeZone` is absent
findings.body: The new conversion computes `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `timeZone` is declared optional on TimeRange (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) and only the slots router's getSchedule populates it. Any other current or future caller of getSlots that passes dateOverrides without a timeZone gets an offset computed against a guessed/local timezone (or a dayjs.tz failure), silently shifting override hours and producing wrong slots — worse than the old behavior, which needed no timezone at all. Additionally, `override.start.toString()` is an unnecessary and lossy round-trip (drops milliseconds, relies on implementation-specific string parsing) since `override.start` is already a Date that dayjs can wrap directly.

findings.title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin scenario the PR claims to fix
findings.body: The PR's primary stated fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events, and its manual test plan describes a round-robin event with one fixed host with a date override. However, the only new automated test extends the single-user 'Check for Date overrides' case with a second timezone. There is no test with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, hosts (isFixed true/false), and a date override on the fixed host, and no test combining a date override with an existing booking — which is exactly why the double-booking regression in checkIfIsAvailable (busy check skipped when dateOverrideExist) is not caught. A test with a fixed host, a date override, and a conflicting booking should be added.
